assessment.nobel_worthiness: Carson's hybrid oeuvre makes scholarship, lyric compression, dramatic address and visual form mutually disruptive sources of literary invention. Its intellectual range serves a highly distinctive poetic voice rather than mere formal display.
assessment.attribution: The proposed citation would recognize Anne Carson for boundary-remaking works that join classical learning, lyric and narrative into singular modern forms.
assessment.maturity: Representative books including Autobiography of Red and Nox indicate a substantial, adventurous body of work whose formal experiment has remained purposeful across decades.
uncertainties: Assessment is necessarily selective across a multiform oeuvre, including works whose visual and performative dimensions are difficult to represent in ordinary reading.
The relative weight to give her classical reworkings versus her original lyric and essay practice remains a critical judgment.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Adonis has made an extensive, consequential intervention in modern Arabic poetry, using myth, fragmentation and dialogue with inherited forms to enlarge its linguistic and imaginative possibilities.
assessment.attribution: The proposed citation would recognize Adonis for renewing Arabic poetic language through sustained modernist invention.
assessment.maturity: Songs of Mihyar the Damascene and A Time Between Ashes and Roses point to a long, coherent poetic project of unusual historical scale.
uncertainties: The committee's access to the full Arabic-language corpus and to its poetic sound and intertextuality is uneven in translation.
The standing of individual phases of the large oeuvre requires careful comparative critical assessment.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Pynchon's encyclopedic fiction has made systems of knowledge, power, technology and countercultural imagination into exuberantly difficult novelistic structures. Its verbal invention and ambition have reshaped possibilities for the English-language novel.
assessment.attribution: The proposed citation would recognize Thomas Pynchon for fiction of extraordinary linguistic and structural imagination that maps modern systems and their discontents.
assessment.maturity: Gravity's Rainbow and Mason & Dixon support the claim of a durable major oeuvre rather than a reputation resting on a single breakthrough.
uncertainties: The density, tonal volatility and scale of the work invite sharply differing judgments about coherence and sustained emotional force.
A full ranking depends on adequate consideration of the less frequently discussed works as well as the major novels.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Cărtărescu's densely patterned prose develops memory, embodiment and imaginative excess into a visionary metaphysical project. Blinding and Solenoid suggest both formal command and an unusually expansive inner world.
assessment.attribution: The proposed citation would recognize Mircea Cărtărescu for visionary fiction that transforms memory and bodily experience into elaborate imaginative architectures.
assessment.maturity: The named major works support an assessment of a mature, sustained project across fiction and poetry.
uncertainties: English-language access to the Romanian corpus and variation among translations limit direct appraisal of its linguistic texture.
The relationship between the maximalist formal method and the total achievement of the oeuvre requires broad corpus coverage.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Hwang's fiction brings divided Korean histories, social worlds and individual lives into layered narrative relation. The Guest and Mater 2-10 indicate a body of work in which historical consciousness is achieved through polyphonic fictional form.
assessment.attribution: The proposed citation would recognize Hwang Sok-yong for fiction that recovers divided histories through layered voices and social worlds.
assessment.maturity: A long career and the range implied by the representative novels support the case for sustained significance rather than topical relevance alone.
uncertainties: Translation availability constrains appraisal of the Korean prose, its registers and the full range of the oeuvre.
The balance between historical witness and formal innovation should be tested across more of the novels.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Tawada turns bilingual estrangement into a generative literary principle, making language itself the site of narrative, poetic and philosophical discovery. Her work combines conceptual clarity with unusual imaginative mobility.
assessment.attribution: The proposed citation would recognize Yoko Tawada for inventive bilingual writing that makes linguistic displacement a source of new narrative and poetic forms.
assessment.maturity: The Emissary and Memoirs of a Polar Bear exemplify a mature cross-genre oeuvre sustained in Japanese and German.
uncertainties: No one translation pathway can fully convey a bilingual practice built from differences between Japanese and German.
The comparative standing of her poetry, drama and essays alongside the fiction requires fuller corpus coverage.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Wright's large-scale narratives renew the novel through Indigenous sovereignty, oral forms and ecological time. Carpentaria and The Swan Book demonstrate an ambitious polyphonic method equal to the historical and environmental worlds it imagines.
assessment.attribution: The proposed citation would recognize Alexis Wright for expansive fiction that remakes narrative form through Indigenous knowledge, communal memory and ecological imagination.
assessment.maturity: The representative novels indicate a substantial and distinctive achievement extending across fiction and nonfiction.
uncertainties: The assessment must avoid reducing complex literary forms to their political or cultural subject matter.
The full formal and linguistic force of oral and local registers may not be equally accessible to all readers.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Can Xue's dreamlike fiction persistently unsettles psychology, space and causality, creating a singularly autonomous narrative world. Frontier and Love in the New Millennium suggest radical formal consistency and imaginative courage.
assessment.attribution: The proposed citation would recognize Can Xue for fiction that expands the imaginative and structural possibilities of narrative through surreal, inward worlds.
assessment.maturity: The named works represent a sustained project rather than an isolated experiment, with a recognizable method developed over a long career.
uncertainties: Translation limits assessment of the Chinese prose's tonal precision and linguistic strangeness.
The demanding opacity of the work produces legitimate disagreement about its range, development and accessibility.
